subject: iceCreamCart
pitch: A cheerful seaside ice cream cart. A mint and cream body with a scalloped striped canopy in pink and white, two big spoked wheels, a push handle, a chrome lid over the freezer, a hand-painted sign shaped like a cone, and a row of giant fake ice cream cones in pastel flavours along the top.
reasoning:
I need to build a single TypeScript module using the agentic-3js-builder SDK, relying only on the documented helper functions since I don't have full API coverage. I'm planning to use the available primitives like joints, chains, sweeps, parts, surfaces, and decals to keep the design reasonably simple but solid.

Since paint, stripes, spots, and svg helpers aren't clearly documented, I'll fall back to plain THREE geometries via b.part with color strings, limited to 64 flat colors, and use b.lathe/b.extrude where shapes need more detail. Since a cart isn't a creature, I'm thinking joints can be minimal—just a root and maybe wheel axle joints for spinning—using the name-first signature for b.joint, and placing parts with b.part(geometry, color, {at, bone}).

For the canopy, I'm planning alternating pink and white box strips to mimic stripes, with half-spheres or half-cylinders along the edge for a scalloped look rather than relying on an unfamiliar lathe outline format. For the ice cream cones, I'll use ConeGeometry rotated to point downward paired with scaled SphereGeometry scoops, since I'm unsure of the exact lathe outline input format and want to avoid that risk.

For a cone-shaped sign, I'm sketching a 2D outline of points approximating a triangle-topped-circle shape to extrude, accepting uncertainty around thickness options, and keeping the hand-painted look simple using colored stripe patterns instead of a texture decal. For the wheels, I'm building a torus tire, cylinder hub, and thin box spokes oriented radially from hub to rim using direction vectors between those points.

I'm settling on a uniform cylinder-based helper function (defined by two endpoints, radius, and color) to build both the handle rod and other connecting parts consistently, plus a flat wide cylinder for the chrome lid. I'm also locking in a pastel color palette (mint, cream, pink, chrome, chocolate, blueberry, waffle-cone tan) and setting the cart's overall scale to roughly 2 meters long and just under 2 meters tall.

Now I'm working out the precise layout: the mint body box sits above the wheels, with a cream rim and a domed chrome freezer lid centered on top, the wheels placed outside the body width with their axle running along X near the back.

For the canopy, I'm planning two support poles rising from the body's front top corners up to a sloped roof, built from alternating pink and white slat boxes stacked across the width and angled outward to form the awning shape.

For the push handle I'll build a U-shape with two posts rising from the body's rear and a crossbar connecting them, since the cart faces +Z this keeps the handle properly at -Z. For the sign, I'm thinking of mounting a cone-shaped outline on the front of the body below the serving window, built from two extrusions (pink fill with a white border) rather than hanging it off the canopy.

Still refining the cone sign shape — a downward-pointing triangle with a scoop sphere on top in tan and pink, placed on the front face at y 0.85, positioned so it clears the canopy above.

Now I'm thinking about decorating the top of the cart with a row of giant inverted ice cream cones along the canopy rim, widening the canopy to about 1.5 units across so five cones spaced 0.3 apart can sit tip-down with scoop spheres on their bases, working out the exact y-center offsets so the cone tips touch the canopy surface at y≈2.05 and the scoops nest just above the cone bases.

I'm also figuring out the bone/joint structure—a root "cart" bone plus wheel joints positioned at the axle locations—and deciding whether to assign wheel parts to those joints via a `bone` option, since I'm not fully certain of the semantics but it seems safest to pass the joint object directly rather than skip bone assignment.

I'm working through the detailed geometry for wheels (tires, rims, hubs, six radial spokes per wheel oriented in the YZ plane), the chassis and mint-colored body with cream trim, the chrome freezer lid dome, front support poles, striped canopy slats with hanging scallops, and a row of oversized ice cream cone decorations along the canopy top with scoops in various flavors. I'm also placing a triangular hand-painted sign with a scoop on top near the front, positioning the serving window and counter shelf, and adding side trim stripes, while finalizing a flat color palette (mint, cream, pink, chrome, dark, tire black, waffle tan, and ice cream flavor colors) for the whole model.

Writing builder helper functions...
